title: Smallest Number in Infinite Set
statement:
Design a data structure `SmallestInfiniteSet` that holds every positive integer `1, 2, 3, ...` when it is created, and supports two operations:

- `popSmallest()` removes the smallest number currently in the set and returns it.
- `addBack(num)` puts the positive integer `num` back into the set. If `num` is already in the set, nothing changes.

The program receives a sequence of operations on one initially full set and must print the result of every `popSmallest` call.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `q`, the number of operations.
Each of the next `q` lines is either `pop` (a call to `popSmallest`) or `add x` (a call to `addBack(x)`).
outputFormat: For every `pop` operation, print the returned number on its own line, in order. `add` operations print nothing. If there is no `pop` operation, print nothing.

examples.input:
7
pop
pop
add 1
pop
add 5
pop
pop
examples.explanation: The pops return 1 and 2. `add 1` puts 1 back, so the next pop returns 1 again. `add 5` does nothing because 5 was never removed. The last two pops return 3 and 4.

examples.input:
6
pop
pop
pop
add 2
add 3
pop
examples.explanation: After three pops, 1, 2 and 3 are removed. Adding 2 and 3 back makes the smallest element 2 again.

hints: Without addBack, the set is always {next, next + 1, ...}, so a single counter `next` describes it.
Numbers that were added back and are smaller than `next` are the exceptions. Keep them in a min-heap.
Guard against duplicates: keep a hash set of the numbers currently in the heap, and ignore addBack(x) when x ≥ next or x is already in the heap.
